At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electrical algebra. At special values of the second type the dimension of the centralizer is the same, but nonzero nilpotent elements appear in it. The $K$-matrices on the sets of special values of the second type are obtained from those already found by substituting the condition, and there are no others. We describe the classical limit, including the limit of special values. We formulate an observation relating the admissibility of a Cartan term to the first homology of the classical subalgebra.

papers.title: Numerical Integration of Geodesic Motion in Non-Schwarzschild Spacetimes
papers.abstract: This contribution presents a method for numerically solving geodesic motion in Wolfram Mathematica applied on a system consisting of a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a thin Vogt-Letelier disk. While geodesic motion in the Schwarzschild spacetime is fully integrable due to its high degree of symmetry, the addition of a disk breaks the spherical symmetry and leads to a weak-integrable dynamical system. Particular attention is paid to the treatment of particle trajectories near the thin disk, where discontinuities in the derivatives of the metric may affect numerical stability and the conservation of integrals of motion. Several numerical treatments of disk crossings were implemented, arriving to a method based on the re-normalization of the four-velocity. The phase-space of the system is investigated using Poincaré sections and rotation number spectra.

papers.title: The chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory: partition functions beyond large-$N$ and quantum holography
papers.abstract: We identify families of Bethe vacua in the chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory whose individual free energies grow as $N^{3/2}$. High-precision data support closed forms for their all-order perturbative $1/N$ expansions. At a distinguished mixed Chern--Simons coupling, the baryonic magnetic flux distinguishes members of this family of vacua. We also study the three-sphere partition function numerically in the 't Hooft limit and Cardy limit, and propose an all-order Airy formula. The four-derivative and one-loop corrections are precision tests of holography.

papers.title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
papers.abstract: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.

papers.title: Radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes in Einstein-phantom scalar-Gauss-Bonnet theory
papers.abstract: We study the radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes found in Einstein--phantom scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial and exponential couplings. Two branches of lower and primary are found for phantom scalarized black holes. The coupled scalar--metric perturbations reduce to a Schrödinger-type equation, after eliminating redundant metric perturbations. The lower branch including the pure quartic solutions has one growing mode, while positive zero-energy solutions for the primary branch could establish stability through the $S$-deformation method. Stable primary solutions are found for the exponential coupling. Also, we explore the connection between radial stability and thermodynamic analysis for two branches. Furthermore, we show that canonical scalarized black holes obtained from Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial coupling reveals unstable lower and stable primary branches.

papers.title: Scalar dynamics in a subclass Ia mimetic DHOST bounce
papers.abstract: We study scalar perturbations in a quadratic subclass Ia degenerate higher-order scalar-tensor (DHOST) realization of a nonsingular bouncing cosmology previously analyzed in higher-derivative mimetic gravity. After a constant rescaling of the scalar potential, the subclass Ia model reproduces the same scale-factor history as the original model, although the associated mimetic Lagrange multiplier generally differs. For the comparison with the original mimetic model, we focus on the branch $0<γ<2/3$, for which the scalar sound speed of the original model is positive. We perform an ADM and Hamiltonian reduction of the scalar sector and show that, imposing the mimetic and momentum constraints, the reduced canonical scalar mode contains no spatial-gradient contribution. The physical scalar sound speed therefore vanishes, $c_s^2=0$, in agreement with the known vacuum behavior of the \(α_L=0\) mimetic-DHOST sector. On the matched bouncing background, the resulting effective frequency squared is independent of the comoving wavenumber and approaches zero from below in the remote contracting phase. Consequently, the asymptotic oscillatory regime used in the previous mimetic model to impose positive-frequency initial conditions is absent. Although canonical normalization can still be imposed through the Wronskian condition, it does not select the initial state uniquely. Without an additional state prescription, the asymptotic dynamics therefore does not uniquely determine the primordial scalar spectrum.

papers.title: Similarity preserving noncommutative maps
papers.abstract: In this note we study similarity preserving automorphisms of noncommutative (NC for short) balls. We show that every similarity preserving NC automorphism is, in fact, given by a similarity with an NC invertible function. As an application, we show that the group of automorphisms of the free semigroup algebra is generated by unitarily implemented and inner automorphisms.

papers.title: Flavor-resolved screening length of a moving quarkonium in a lattice-calibrated holographic QCD plasma
papers.abstract: We compute the screening length \(L_s\) of a moving heavy quark-antiquark pair in a lattice-calibrated Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton background for pure-glue, two-flavor, and \(2+1\)-flavor matter. Parallel and perpendicular orientations are considered at finite temperature, baryon chemical potential, and rapidity. \(L_s\) decreases monotonically with \(T\) and \(η\) in every flavor sector, and for the flavored systems also with \(μ\). The perpendicular screening length is systematically smaller than the parallel one. At zero density and \(T=0.3\ \mathrm{GeV}\), the ordering \(L_s^{(N_f=0)}>L_s^{(N_f=2)}>L_s^{(N_f=2+1)}\) holds in this calibration, and a lattice check of the static flavor dependence is proposed. At finite density the two-flavor and \(2+1\)-flavor curves cross along a line in the \(T\)-\(μ\) plane; below the line \(L_s^{(N_f=2)}>L_s^{(N_f=2+1)}\), while above it the ordering reverses. The crossing follows from the competition between the two-flavor crossover temperature and the density coupling, and its location depends on the fitted parameters. These results provide a flavor-resolved reference for moving quarkonium screening in the baryon-rich regime probed by beam energy scans.

papers.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
papers.abstract: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. However, performing such simulations long enough to relax the magnetohydrodynamics near the BBHs is computationally challenging and a source of uncertainty in modeling efforts. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000 \, GM/c^3$), relaxing the magnetic field dynamics within the CBD cavity. After $\sim 23$ orbits and persistent magnetically arrested minidisks, the accretion enters a new magnetically arrested mode which we call dual horizon-MAD (DH-MAD). In DH-MAD, the dimensionless horizon magnetic fluxes remain saturated at $φ_{BH}\sim 20$ driving magnetic flux eruptions from the vicinity of the BH horizons, and the vertical magnetic flux in the cavity saturates, but no flux eruptions occur at the cavity-CBD boundary. During this DH-MAD phase, there is also a shift in the total mass accretion rate variability, which exhibits a periodicity of $f\sim 1.8 f_{\rm orb}$, while the accretion rate modulation on the individual black holes occurs almost at the orbital period, $f\sim 0.9 f_{\rm orb}$. $φ_{BH}$ also exhibits a robust periodicity at $f\sim 0.4 f_{\rm orb}$, suggesting that quasiperiodic nonthermal emission from magnetic reconnection near the horizons could be a smoking gun electromagnetic counterpart to inspiraling SMBBHs. Finally, minidisks around the BHs become intermittent in the DH-MAD phase, even at a separation of $d/M = 24$, likely due to the large plasma magnetization in the optically thin cavity.

papers.title: Higgs-portal dark matter beyond kinetic equilibrium
papers.abstract: We revisit the scalar, vector, and fermion Higgs-portal dark matter models in the resonant regime without assuming kinetic equilibrium during the freeze-out. We compute the relic abundance by solving the full momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation and compare the results with the standard momentum-averaged treatment. We find that the standard treatment significantly underestimates the relic abundance below the resonance, apart from the fermionic case with a purely scalar portal coupling where the difference is negligible. The deviation from the standard treatment is largest for fermionic models with pseudoscalar interactions, corresponding to factor of 10 in terms of the coupling that reproduces the correct relic abundance. For the scalar and vector cases the corresponding difference is up to a factor of 2. We confront the resulting parameter space with the latest constraints from direct and indirect detection, as well as collider experiments. We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.

papers.title: Scotogenic dark matter from gauged $L_μ+L_τ$
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce the first scotogenic model based on a gauged $L_μ + L_τ$ symmetry whose spontaneous breaking by two units leaves a remnant matter parity $M_P$. The resulting light active neutrinos are of Majorana nature and the lightest electrically neutral state mediating the scotogenic loop is stabilized by $M_P$ and can be identified as a weakly interacting massive particle dark matter candidate. We analyze the phenomenology of a predominantly singlet-like CP-even scalar dark matter candidate and the representative regions of parameter space compatible with the observed thermal relic abundance. The $Z'$ boson is compatible with a broad range of parameters relevant for dark matter. In particular, electroweak precision constraints do not lead to significant tensions for kinetic mixing values up to $ε\sim 10^{-2}$. We discuss the implications of existing searches for leptophilic gauge bosons and the conditions under which visible and invisible collider signatures become relevant.

papers.title: WIMPs as FIMPs: the Inert Doublet Model and low-temperature reheating
papers.abstract: Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) are conventionally assumed to acquire their dark matter relic abundance through thermal freeze-out. However, this association relies on assumptions concerning the thermal history of the early Universe. We revisit the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), a representative WIMP framework in which dark matter interacts with the Standard Model through electroweak gauge interactions, even when its Higgs-portal coupling vanishes. We demonstrate that sufficiently low reheating temperatures can prevent chemical equilibrium, allowing a genuine WIMP to acquire its relic abundance through freeze-in rather than freeze-out. Considering both instantaneous and finite-duration reheating, we identify different production histories, including freeze-out during radiation domination, freeze-out during reheating, and freeze-in with potentially significant annihilation backreactions. These scenarios open regions of the IDM parameter space that would otherwise be excluded by dark matter overabundance. Our results demonstrate that WIMPs can behave as FIMPs, depending on the thermal history of the Universe.

papers.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
papers.abstract: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as $S \lesssim \sqrt{B}$. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX-4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark-electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT, and XLZD. We find that dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.

papers.title: Wormholes do not contribute to supersymmetric partition functions
papers.abstract: We show that wormholes connecting multiple asymptotic boundaries always spontaneously break at least some of the symmetries preserved by their boundary conditions. Their configurations then form nontrivial orbits of the broken symmetry, and for the case of a fermionic symmetry, the contribution of each orbit vanishes. We conclude that wormholes do not contribute to moments of supersymmetric partition functions. This extends results on supersymmetric indices by Iliesiu, Kologlu, and Turiaci. We emphasize that supersymmetric partition functions can still have a nonzero ensemble variance. In SYK-like examples that we analyze, this arises due to the contribution of ``non-geometric wormhole'' configurations that preserve all continuous symmetries.

papers.title: Level repulsion and the quantum viscosity of near-extremal black branes
papers.abstract: Below the gap scale of the AdS$_2$ throat, quantum fluctuations make the shear viscosity of near-extremal black branes grow as $(CT)^{-1/2}$ in the disk approximation of JT gravity, and the one-loop $η/s$ diverges. To cure this divergence, we include the non-perturbative completion of JT gravity as a matrix integral. The Kubo formula then probes universal features of level correlations. At finite extremal entropy $S_0$, level repulsion makes the DC viscosity vanish. A finite, universal viscosity survives in a double-scaling limit in which the probe frequency $ω$ is held in a fixed ratio to the level-spacing scale $ω_{\rm sp}\equiv e^{-S_0}/C$. At fixed $ω$, with $ω_{\rm sp}\llω\ll e^{S_0/3}ω_{\rm sp}$ the Schwarzian growth then saturates at $η_{\max}\simeq0.174\,(ω/ω_{\rm sp})\,η_{sc}$, where $η_{sc}$ is the semiclassical viscosity, and the viscosity decreases at lower temperatures. At the extremely low temperature scale $CT\sim e^{-2S_0/3}$ the genus expansion and the one-loop entropy computations completely break down. There we start probing the edge of the spectrum and the problem reduces exactly to the Airy kernel. We find that the ratio of the quenched averages of $η$ and $s$ is finite and positive at every non-zero temperature. We compare our results with explicit completions defined by the string equation, in which the spectrum is bounded from below. The bulk results are the same in these completions and the quenched edge results change only by a few per cent, while the annealed quantities depend on the non-perturbative completion at order one.

papers.title: Ohmic warm inflation
papers.abstract: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.

papers.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
papers.abstract: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.

papers.title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
papers.abstract: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.

papers.title: Autonomous quantum machine learning via Riemannian gradient-based optimization
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning models typically rely on repeated quantum measurements and classical optimization during training, making the quantum-to-classical information-extraction process a fundamental bottleneck for scalability. We propose a framework for autonomous self-training quantum machine learning, based on Riemannian gradient optimization, in which the optimization proceeds entirely within the quantum domain without requiring quantum measurements or classical feedback. We derive the Riemannian gradient update rules for a broad class of learning tasks and identify sufficient conditions under which the resulting training dynamics can be realized fully autonomously. Within this regime, we establish an exponential convergence guarantee, in the training iterations, for sufficiently small step sizes, and further analyze the training cost in terms of the growth of the circuit depth. Importantly, we further show that the trained model can automatically discover symmetries hidden in the training data without $\textit{a priori}$ specification. For the canonical examples of quantum phase classification and unitary learning with a hidden symmetry, our numerical study indicates that learning can be achieved at low circuit depths with only a few distinct training examples. Our results thus establish autonomous quantum machine learning as a promising paradigm that removes the classical optimization loop while retaining strong theoretical guarantees and practical performances.

papers.title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
papers.abstract: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.

papers.title: Riemannian Curvature Functionals for de Rham Spectral Triples
papers.abstract: We compute mixed Clifford residue functionals for the Hodge-de Rham operator in even dimensions. A symbol-composition calculation recovers the Riemann and Einstein tensors and yields two ordered curvature functionals with the same classical limit. For specified truncation products on warped collars, we evaluate all five boundary cases and prove that the curvature-recovering antisymmetrizations have no boundary correction. We extend the constructions to spectral data equipped with two one-form actions. Explicit noncommutative torus and finite-direction examples distinguish the functionals and exhibit failures of module balancing and Riemann symmetries. A conformal example shows that a naive exterior lift need not recover classical curvature. The additional structures and limitations of each extension are stated explicitly.

papers.title: Polarized IKKT holography: bulk realization of BPS operators
papers.abstract: We study the holographic imprint of polarization in the lowest BPS multiplet of the IKKT matrix model. On the matrix model side, the deformation requires operator mixing and broken-symmetry Ward identities to organize the surviving operators into an irreducible atypical multiplet of the $F(4)$ superalgebra. In the bulk, we use one-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity to identify the analytic half-BPS background with $F(4)$ symmetry whose boundary behavior matches the IKKT polarization. We solve the linearized bosonic and fermionic equations around this background and its undeformed counterpart exactly, and extract the independent asymptotic data. The supersymmetry transformations of these data reproduce the matrix model multiplets, thus establishing a bulk realization of this BPS operator structure.

papers.title: A local symmetry forces positivity for projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metrics
papers.abstract: We prove that a projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metric has positive Einstein constant as soon as it admits one nonzero local real-holomorphic Killing field. Neither completeness nor a prescribed global group action is assumed. This gives a partial answer, under a local symmetry hypothesis, to the general positivity problem for Kahler-Einstein submanifolds of (finite-dimensional) projective space. The key observation is that, by Calabi rigidity, a local real-holomorphic Killing field is induced by a projective unitary vector field whose tangency propagates along any connected global Kahler immersion, without a simple-connectivity assumption. Applied to Hulin's complete continuation, this produces a global Killing field with a bounded Hamiltonian potential given by the ambient projective moment map. The resulting Laplace equation, the Omori--Yau maximum principle and Yau's Liouville theorem exclude both negative and zero Einstein curvature. We also prove a non-Einstein obstruction under uniformly negative Ricci curvature and obtain compact equivariant continuations.

papers.title: On a Supersymmetric Generalization of the Matytsin Formula
papers.abstract: We derive the leading asymptotics of the supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for the supergroup $U(n|m)$ in the limit $n,m\to\infty$ when $n/m$ is kept finite. This generalizes the Matytsin result for $U(N)$. We show that it is described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to the bosonic and fermionic sectors.

papers.title: Calabi-Yau at 50: mathematical discovery in the age of AI
papers.abstract: Using the golden jubilee of Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture as a spring-board, we discuss how the dataset of Calabi-Yau manifolds brought together mathematicians and physicists since the 1980s, and then further brought in the world of machine-learning and AI since 2017. We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid.

papers.title: Onset of quantum chaos in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories
papers.abstract: We exhibit random matrix statistics in the scaling dimensions of non-BPS primary operators in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories. Specifically, we consider the sigma model with K3 target space and $\mathcal N=(4,4)$ supersymmetry in a neighborhood of the Kummer orbifold point $\mathbb T^4/\mathbb Z_2$. At the free-fermion radius, the spin-zero spectrum of the $\mathbb Z_2^4$-invariant sector is exactly degenerate at integer energies. The exactly marginal blow-up deformations that preserve this symmetry form a four-dimensional space, whose directions we parametrize by unit quaternions. Along each deformation direction, we compute the first-order splitting of the degenerate levels, i.e., the leading anomalous dimensions as the coupling goes to zero. In sectors where all exact symmetries are resolved, including a hidden $\mathbb Z_2$ at the even levels, the non-zero first-order shifts along a generic direction follow the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE), as we verify by computing several spectral diagnostics. We compare quantitatively with the well-known singlet deformation, which has enhanced symmetry: even after all its known symmetries are resolved, its first-order spectrum has exact degeneracies, its gap ratio approaches the GOE value only slowly as the energy increases, and its unfolded spectrum lacks the long-range rigidity of the GOE.

papers.title: A matrix model of an M5--brane on a plane--wave background
papers.abstract: We construct the maximally supersymmetric deformation of the recently proposed $\mathcal{A}_6$ matrix model on a plane--wave background. We derive the same theory independently, by reducing the light--cone M5--brane on a five--sphere in this background to its lowest harmonics, including the dynamics of its chiral two--form and of its fermions. We then classify all its classical vacua. We show that one of them is the fivebrane giant graviton, and that its fluctuations form a single $\mathfrak{su}(2|4)$ multiplet, which reproduces the $\ell=1$ level of the spherical transverse fivebrane identified in the large $N$ limit of BMN theory. Moreover, the dynamical tensor supports new families of vacua, where the flux balances the size of the brane, and whose spectrum contains that of a fuzzy membrane. Finally, we show that BLG theory sits inside the model, both on a Coulomb branch of the massless theory and around the giant graviton of the massive one, where the two membranes are polarized into the fivebrane.

papers.title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
papers.abstract: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_φ\lesssim 10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$. For $m_φ\gtrsim10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$, repulsive self-interactions narrow the density distribution, reducing the deviation of the survival probability at the first minimum to $ΔP \approx 0.07$ for an appropriate self-interaction coupling. In contrast, for a real scalar field, rapid oscillations with the Compton frequency distort the probabilities for scalar masses $ 10^{-22}~\mathrm{eV} \lesssim m_φ\lesssim 10^{-10} ~\mathrm{eV}$, and self-interactions do not remove this distortion. This distortion becomes negligible only for $m_φ\gtrsim10^{-9}~\mathrm{eV}$. We explore additional effects which could modify the interference pattern and relax the constraints on the required values of $m_φ$. These include scenarios with multiple scalar fields (the axiverse), the gravitational effects of the Sun and Earth on the granule structure, and interactions with the relic neutrino background.

papers.title: Super quantum groups of divided powers à la Lusztig
papers.abstract: We construct super analogues of the quantum groups of divided powers introduced by Lusztig. We call them super analogues because the Lie-theoretical data governing their structure is comparable to that of contragredient Lie superalgebras. Indeed, we show that they admit PBW-type bases parametrized by root systems of super type, and that they also have Lusztig isomorphisms giving a representation of the corresponding Weyl groupoids. Moreover, we prove that our super objects are equipped with a Frobenius-type morphism whose kernel is the Drinfeld double of a finite-dimensional Nichols algebra of super type, a super analogue of Lusztig's small quantum group, and whose cokernel is the enveloping algebra of the semisimple Lie algebra determined by the Cartan roots of the Nichols algebra. We carry out our construction within the framework of Nichols algebras of diagonal type, specifically, those whose braiding is obtained by specializing at a root of unity. This allows us to consider a divided power integral form inside a large quantum group of De Concini--Kac--Procesi type and then, via specialization, obtain our desired object.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic R-matrix from Hasse diagrams
papers.abstract: We calculate R-matrix in the basic representation for the ortho-symplectic quantum supergroups in arbitrary polarizations, by a method of Hasse diagrams.

papers.title: Exact Spherical Branes and Deformations: BMN, IKKT and $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$
papers.abstract: We present a unified analytic solution to the BPS equations of spherical Dp-branes for $1\leq p \leq 5$ and give the corresponding type II uplifts in closed form. These are holographically dual to maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^{p+1}$. The change of variables that makes the BPS equations integrable also allows us to analytically calculate a universal result for the holographic Wilson loop and obtain UV asymptotic behaviour previously determined numerically. The same change of variables extends naturally, with suitable modifications, to the cases $p=0$ and $p=-1$. We obtain a 1-parameter family of D0-brane solutions and show how the IR conditions lead to a singular limit of the integration constant. We also solve the D(-1)-brane BPS equations and show the resulting Euclidean uplift fails regularity conditions. Separately, we obtain an explicit representation of the one-ball electrostatic solution of polarised IKKT, which lets us express multipole moments and holographic observables using elliptic invariants. Finally, we analytically solve the BPS equations of the holographic dual of $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^4$, present the corresponding type IIB uplift and calculate the holographic Wilson loop.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
papers.abstract: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser processing conditions with material thermophysical properties, improve melt pool prediction over raw process parameters. We systematically benchmark seven models: four classical ML methods (Gaussian process, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) and three pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabDPT, and TabICLv2). Experiments span 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets, covering regression of melt pool width and depth and classification of melting modes. Dimensionless features yield comparable or superior predictive performance in most settings, with the largest gains in cross-material depth prediction (R^2 = 0.96). Tabular foundation models generally achieve stronger classification performance than classical baselines, particularly for multi-material datasets. These findings indicate that combining physically meaningful dimensionless representations with pretrained tabular models can improve data-efficient melt pool modeling and support more transferable process-window identification in LPBF.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography
papers.abstract: Objective: Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE) is a non-invasive imaging technique for mapping biomechanical properties of in vivo tissue, including shear wave speed (SWS), but involves intrinsically slow data acquisition and an ill-posed wave inversion. Instead of relying on handcrafted image priors, we propose a data-driven approach jointly combining image reconstruction and MRE inversion for robust SWS estimation from undersampled k-space data. Methods: Our physics-informed reconstruction framework comprises two blocks: a model-based neural network (NN)-regularized reconstruction module and a phase-gradient inversion (k-MDEV) calculating SWS from the reconstructed images. Concatenating both blocks yields an end-to-end trainable method to estimate SWS directly from measured k-space data. We evaluated the method on retrospectively highly undersampled brain MRE data and compared it to a total variation (TV) minimization-based approach. We assessed the impact of end-to-end training (qualitative images and SWS maps as targets) versus pre-training (qualitative images as targets) and applied the method also to in vivo data. Results: Our approach significantly reduces NRMSE by 30% compared to TV. End-to-end training improves SWS estimation over separate image reconstruction and SWS calculation. Conclusion: Accurate SWS quantification is possible at acceleration factors up to 19. Our method significantly outperforms TV, highlighting the need for data-driven regularization in this challenging MR problem. Further, our approach successfully generalizes to in vivo data. Significance: We present the first end-to-end trainable MRE reconstruction method for estimating SWS maps directly from k-space. NN-based reconstruction can enable rapid stiffness mapping for dynamic studies, functional imaging, and real-time clinical feedback.

papers.title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
papers.abstract: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. The construction is generalized to the $p=2n-1$ family, with local dimensions supporting absolutely maximally entangled states. On finite networks satisfying a radial orientation condition, an appropriate normalization produces an isometric bulk--boundary map. For cuts satisfying the isometry condition on both sides, the boundary entropy decomposes into a link contribution $\sum_{\ell}\log(2j_{\ell}+1)$ and the bulk entropy, thereby providing a discrete realization of the quantum Ryu--Takayanagi structure. Applications to the black hole interior are formulated via postselection-based non-isometric encoding. Assuming additional Haar statistics, this framework is used to analyze the preservation of overlaps on average and the competition between entropy branches underlying the Page Curve. These results establish a constructive link between the geometric degrees of freedom of LQG and holographic codes, while clarifying the conditions required to connect them to geometric area in LQG, the location of the quantum extremal surface, and evaporation of black hole.

papers.title: Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices
papers.abstract: We study the local eigenvalue correlations of products of independent induced symplectic Ginibre matrices in the large-dimensional limit. We establish the scaling limits of the correlation functions in the bulk, at the spectral edges, and outside the limiting spectral support, both near and away from the real axis. At regular spectral points, we show that the limiting correlations coincide with those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble, exhibiting Pfaffian structures near the real axis and determinantal structures away from it. At the origin, where the limiting spectral density develops a singularity, we derive an integral representation of the parameter-dependent limiting Pfaffian prekernel. Our proofs are based on a unified approach involving a differential equation for the skew prekernels and their asymptotics.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
papers.abstract: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate that searches of the Fermi-GBM archive and a future MeV gamma-ray mission such as COSI could detect these bursts. We also discuss possible multimessenger counterparts, including fast radio bursts powered by magnetic energy release, kilonovae and $511\,{\rm keV}$ line emission associated with centrifugally ejected neutron-rich matter, and gravitational waves from the rapid collapse and subsequent black-hole ringdown. Together, these signals probe complementary stages of PBH-induced NS consumption.

papers.title: Noncompactifiable Kähler threefolds with positive Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: We construct a complete Kähler threefold $(M,ω)$ with positive Ricci curvature and infinite-dimensional third rational homology. It admits no analytic compactification, answering Yau's compactification question negatively (see \cite{Yau1992}, Problem~71, p.~304). The metric is obtained by solving a complex Monge--Ampère equation on an affine threefold and lifting the solution to an infinite cyclic cover. Its Ricci form $ρ_ω$ satisfies $\int_Mρ_ω^3=\infty$, disproving the top Yang--Yau conjecture.

papers.title: The geometry of neural network decision boundaries
papers.abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are built using well-understood mathematical operations, yet their complex nature poses significant challenges to intuitively understanding their decision-making processes. This work introduces a method for visualizing and measuring ANN decision boundary geometry directly in the high-dimensional input space, avoiding distortions found with traditional projection-based techniques. We analyze boundary curvatures and distances in diverse inputs, architectures, and training methods. Boundary distances grow smoothly and slowly with consistent curvature as the size of the subspace increases, suggesting that decision boundaries are close to input samples within large, continuous subspaces. We also quantify how much boundary distances and curvatures reduce near dataset samples after adversarial training. Training methodology has a significantly stronger impact on boundary distance and curvature than architecture or test-set accuracy. These findings are contextualized within prior work, supporting or refuting several previously proposed theories of boundary behavior. Our analytically and empirically supported methodology lays the foundation for future studies to improve network interpretability and understanding.

papers.title: PANO: Parallel Latent Space Neural Operator for Solving PDEs
papers.abstract: Aggregating observations into a limited number of latent tokens and learning physical interactions in the latent space has emerged as an effective approach for Transformer-based neural operators to solve Partial Differential Equation (PDE) problems involving large-scale observations. However, existing methods typically compress observations using a single aggregation pattern, making physical information not retained by that pattern invisible to the latent space and thereby constraining physical interactions within it. To address this limitation, we propose PArallel Latent Space Neural Operator (PANO), a novel neural operator for solving PDEs that formulates physical interactions among observations as an additive combination of interaction results from parallel latent spaces with shared parameters. Specifically, PANO transforms observations into multiple distinct compressed representations through independent mappings, learns physical interactions in parallel based on these representations, and finally fuses the decoded results to predict the target physical field. Within PANO, we further propose Coupled Assignment Projection (CAP) to construct bidirectionally consistent encoding and decoding mappings, and Pairwise Latent Space Attention Layer (PaLA) to jointly update latent representations of each latent space through adaptive cross-space interactions. Extensive experiments on nine benchmarks spanning diverse physical systems, geometries, and observation scales demonstrate that PANO achieves state-of-the-art performance. Notably, PANO reduces equivalent plastic strain prediction errors on Unilateral Stamping by 28.3% (or more) and lift-coefficient prediction errors on AirCraft by 21.4% (or more) compared with existing methods. Code is available at https://github.com/ZijiangY1116/PANO.

papers.title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Linear probes are the cheapest LLM lie detectors but often fail to transfer across kinds of lie. Label-free directions from honest and deceptive role-play are untested at 70B scale and on lies about knowledge, where a lie and an honest denial can be identical. We widen a published persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they have, plus honest counterparts. At each model's middle layer the resulting persona direction ranks lies across Liars' Bench better than single-dataset probes on three of its four models; it fails on Qwen, even when Qwen stays in role far more often. On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct it beats directions from a random persona bank, but its gain over the published direction is within the range of random widenings. On lies about knowledge, persona directions mainly track a reply's wording: where lies and honest denials share their words, our three main contrasts stay inside the random-direction band on Llama and Qwen and reach only its edge on Gemma, though on Mistral one clears it. A knowledge direction contrasts questions the model can answer with ones nobody can, each followed by the same scripted denial. It separates lies from identical honest denials on two models and narrowly on a third, but not on the fourth; its other results partly depend on the benchmark's wording. On the Gender-Secret fine-tune it clears the band by a few hundredths on Llama and fails on Mistral. The sum of the two directions ranks lies better than a supervised probe at the same depth on all four models (on one, both near chance) but is level with the persona direction on Llama's average and behind that probe on held-out lies. More varied role-play questions do not help the persona direction on Liars' Bench.

papers.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential data remain comparatively understudied, largely because they are difficult to train. In this work, we present a rigorous benchmark of variational quantum recurrent neural networks (QRNNs) on time series prediction tasks, focusing on two key capabilities: memory and nonlinear processing. We introduce a task-driven methodology that quantifies model capacity, enabling an intuitive and fair comparison across architectures, including classical recurrent baselines. We evaluate the proposed framework on two generic benchmark tasks and on a synthetic dataset describing a chaotic system. Overall, the quantum models achieve performance comparable to their classical counterparts, but classical models scale better with the memory size within the range studied. Notably, one QRNN variant shows higher average capacity on the task designed to jointly probe memory and nonlinear capacity. Moreover, our results show that quantum models offer better capacity when we are able to find a good parameter initialization. However, the increasing sensitivity to initialization leads to a lower probability of finding good solutions as the model size increases. These results provide a principled starting point for designing richer quantum recurrent architectures and for assessing where they may offer practical benefits.

papers.title: Learning from Duality in Neural Network Field Theories
papers.abstract: We develop neural realizations of positive-level Wess-Zumino-Witten models using bosonic Wakimoto and fermionic Fourier-Berezin fields. Level-rank duality connects the charged sectors of the fermionic construction, where explicit neural observables recover conformal block data and enable the transfer of information about unknown correlators between paired theories. We also show that distinct neural presentations of the same continuum current algebra exhibit different finite-width behavior, with approximation accuracy depending on architecture, regulator, and parameter distribution. These results connect the exact mathematical structure of conformal field theory with the expressive and computational properties of neural field theories.

papers.title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
papers.abstract: Physics-informed operator learning trains neural operators on the residual of a parametric partial differential equation (PDE) instead of labeled solution data, but its reliability depends on a variationally correct residual: one that is equivalent to the error in a norm dictated by the equation, the PDE-compliant norm. For nonlinear equations written as first-order systems, we prove that the first-order system least-squares residual is equivalent to the error in this norm near a solution branch if the linearized residual is stable and the residual derivative is Lipschitz continuous, possibly in a norm stronger than the error norm. We verify these conditions for monotone reaction, solution- and gradient-dependent diffusion, and compressible Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity. The stability mechanisms vary across these classes, as do the regions where the equivalence holds, from arbitrary bounded sets to a neighborhood of the branch. In a conforming finite element space, we show that the loss excess of a state near the finite element solution is equivalent to its squared distance from that solution. We use this loss to train a reduced basis neural operator with values in this space, with solution snapshots needed only for the basis and the loss and its symbolically derived gradient assembled by the finite element library. At inference, this loss estimates the error. Numerically, the square root of the loss excess tracks the error within factors comparable to those of the linear case, and the operator achieves higher accuracy in the PDE-compliant norm than grid-based baselines evaluated in the same finite element space.

papers.title: Efficient Modeling of Multi-Agent Systems via Structure-Aware Physics-Informed Learning
papers.abstract: Modeling large multi-agent systems poses challenges for trajectory inference and parameter identification, as network size and coupling increase computational demands and partial observations require reconstructing unobserved states. We propose MAS-PINN, a neural-network architecture with a tailored training algorithm for a physics-informed learning framework that leverages the network topology and the agents' similarity to reduce computational and memory costs of simulating and identifying multi-agent systems. Its architecture represents agent trajectories through shared temporal features and agent-specific coefficients. Training alternates between learning features, fitting coupled trajectories, and estimating physical parameters. A matrix-free update exploits local interactions to fit trajectories without forming large global matrices. Experiments on Lorenz rings, Lotka--Volterra networks, and Rössler oscillators show improved trajectory and parameter accuracy over baselines, including inference in large systems and identification under partial observations or unknown topology, alongside substantial computational savings in coefficient fitting.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly. The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students. The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.

papers.title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
papers.abstract: Physics simulation outputs increasingly come from solvers that no expert inspects, such as third-party packages in automated pipelines, programs written by large language models (LLMs), and learned surrogates. In earlier work on cardiac pulsed field ablation, we proposed that solvers return a certificate with their answers. The certificate consists of an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current, and a small independent checker turns it into guaranteed error bounds against a written specification of the physics. Here, the same checker verifies the outputs of other solvers on the same problem. Specifically, FEniCSx computes both fields and receives the same bounds as our own solver. Five plausible bugs in a correct solver, one of them about 0.2% from the true impedance, all converge and pass a grid convergence study, yet the certificate rejects or refutes all five. Of three solvers written by LLMs, one is correct and certified to 0.1%, and one never solves the equation but converges. Neural networks that predict the coefficients of a reduced basis emit admissible fields and receive valid per-prediction bounds, at most 0.0021% wide inside their training range and 0.3-25% wide outside it, where 90% conformal intervals cover none of 14 tests. Untuned Fourier neural operators with free nodal outputs receive valid but uninformative bounds. On a uniform grid, interpolation onto the certificate grid limits them, and on the certificate grid, thin cells turn small nodal errors into large energy errors. Energy-norm training narrows the certified interval tenfold, and projecting the nodal-loss outputs onto the reduced basis narrows it by two to four orders of magnitude, still uninformative. The guarantee concerns the stated model and holds for any output, wherever its input lies. It is informative only when the output is accurate in energy on a grid that resolves the problem.

papers.title: Vitrify Exact Learning: exact differential equations, changes of variable and closed forms from numerical data
papers.abstract: Symbolic regression searches a space of expression trees for a formula that fits data. Many functions of the sciences have no finite expression over the usual operations and still satisfy a linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients. Vitrify Exact Learning takes nu- merical values of a function and proceeds in three steps. It assumes that the function, in its own variable or after a change of variable or a pushforward of a density, is annihilated by an operator with polynomial coefficients. It finds that operator as the null vector of a matrix of weak-form measurements, in which the data are integrated against test functions and never differentiated, makes the coefficients exact, and tests the exact operator on data that the fit did not read against a noise level propagated from the data. It then solves the exact operator symbolically and keeps the closed form that matches the data. Each step has precedent; the combination takes values on an interval, from a quadrature, a float64 table or a sample, to an exact equation and a closed form. On noise-free benchmarks it recovers 45 of 53 classic targets, 108 of the 120 AI Feynman equations and 74.1% of the Feynman problems of SR- Bench, against 33, 69 and 55.8% for the best other programs, and 50 of 132 special-function targets generated after its code was frozen, against 23. From 40-digit values it returns Meijer G densities, hypergeometric forms for the deflection of light by a black hole, and Appell and Lauricella functions of two variables. With noise in several variables, with sparse data and for equations above fourth order it mostly returns no model.

papers.title: Random Feature Neural Networks for Stochastic Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Random feature neural networks (RFNNs) sample their hidden parameters once and train only the output layer. We analyze RFNNs as feedback policies for finite-horizon stochastic control with trajectory-dependent objectives. A policy change alters later states, so the error that matters is the objective error of the induced trajectory rather than a pointwise regression error. We extend the quantitative random-feature approximation theory for PDE solutions and nonlinear regression to feedback control. We investigate the objective error of an RFNN policy through two sources, approximation of the policy by random features and estimation of the objective from finitely many paths. A stability estimate for the controlled trajectory turns a policy error into an objective error. Under bounded actions, a regular benchmark policy and exact empirical minimization, the expected objective gap to the benchmark policy is at most of order $N^{-1/2}+\sqrt{N(1+\log N)/n}$, with $N$ the feature width per output coordinate and $n$ the number of paths. At fixed sample size the two terms trade off in $N$, and balancing them gives $N\asymp\sqrt{n/\log n}$. Across a wide range of examples, estimated gaps generally decrease with width and sample size, and RFNNs show an advantage when simulated paths are limited. We also study Parsimonious Random Feature Learning (PRFL), which grows and prunes the random dictionary during training while training only the output coefficients. At matched retained width and training budget, PRFL improves on a fixed RFNN in the LQ and Heston comparisons, while the fully trained network remains best in those examples.
